title: finding(app-shell tests): a FOURTH foreign-target `tree` fixture that both sweeps are blind to — `expandableFamily.identity-5874` builds it through a `field('tree')` factory, so neither the target-key grep nor the `type: 'tree'` emit scan sees it
body:
Found by re-running objectui#8031's shape scan **as a shape scan**, at the dispatching seat's explicit instruction to re-derive the population before declaring three — and it is the fourth. Verified line by line by the reviewing seat before filing.

## What

`packages/app-shell/src/utils/expandableFamily.identity-5874.test.ts` builds every fixture field through a factory that takes the field type as an argument and attaches the same target to all of them:

| line | reading |
|---|---|
| `:122` | `reference: 'accounts',` — inside the shared `field()` factory |
| `:134`, `:137` | `objectName: 'deal'` / `name: 'deal'` — the declaring object's identity |
| `:142` | `parent_node: field('tree'),` |
| `:210` | `expect(out.referenceTo).toBe('accounts');` |

⇒ a `tree` field whose target names **another object** (`deal` declaring, `accounts` targeted), in the **canonical** spelling.

## ⭐ Why BOTH previous sweeps were blind to it, which is the point of the card

- objectui#7839's sweep was keyed on the **target key**. Here the key sits inside a shared factory with no `tree` in sight — the grep lands on a helper.
- objectui#8031's sweep was keyed on `type: 'tree'` **emits**. Here the type is an **argument**, `field('tree')`, so there is no literal `type: 'tree'` to match.

⇒ **the population is defined by neither spelling.** Triage's own lesson on objectui#8031 was *"a population defined by a spelling is not the population defined by the shape"*; this instance shows the shape scan needs one more turn of the same screw — a factory call is a shape a text scan does not see either.

⭐ And it is the live counterexample that makes objectui#8031's pin answer sound: a gate keyed on literal `type: 'tree'` emits would have gone **green** while this stayed open.

## ⛔ NOT the same disposition as objectui#8031's three

Those three were dropped because the key was **inert** — refused at parse, read by nobody, annotating nothing. **Here the target is load-bearing**: `:210` asserts `referenceTo` is `'accounts'` for the tree row, so dropping the key turns the suite red.

⇒ a fix has to **choose**, and that is why this is a card and not a drive-by:

- rename the tree row's target to the declaring object (`deal`) and move that assertion; or
- split the shared `field()` helper so the tree member can carry a different target from the lookup family.

⛔ Neither is picked here. ⚠️ And note the second option touches a helper every field in the fixture flows through, so its blast radius inside this suite is larger than it looks.

## What is and is not refused today

⚠️ Measured on the installed pin, `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, with a nonsense-key negative control: a `tree` field with a declared `reference` naming **another** object is **ACCEPTED** — `refuseForeignTreeReference` landed on objectstack `main` **after** this pin was cut. ⇒ this fixture is refused **upstream**, ⛔ not by the copy this repo installs today.

⭐ That makes this a **latent** card rather than a live one, and the grading should say so: it goes live the day objectui bumps to a spec that carries the refusal, and on that day it is a red suite rather than a finding.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether other fixtures in this repo build fields through a type-argument factory the same way — only this one was found, and finding it was a by-product rather than a census. ⛔ Whether the `field()` helper is shared beyond this file. ⛔ Which of the two remedies costs less; no attempt was made.

⚠️ Recorded so the next enumeration does not re-derive it: the two remaining `type: 'tree'` emits that carry a declared target — plugin-tree's `expandFls-7429` and `settledSchemaKeying-6481` — were checked and are **legal self-references**, and the deliberately foreign arms in objectui#7839's own suite are that suite's subject matter and must stay.

Refs: objectui#8031 (the three whose scan found this, and whose pin answer this justifies) · objectui#7839 (the original four, and the sweep keyed on the target key) · objectui#5874 (the card this fixture pins).
